reason: Feasibility is fine: it is a rule with no runtime, trivially byte-identical, not a mechanism under R8, and it can still be logged before the 43/44 scores (both PENDING at 05:47Z, expected ~12:40-13:10Z). The VALUE case does not hold. (1) The files are nested. The DC threshold is a veto on safe-division candidates, followed by a greedy pass with caps (experiments/ext_corwin-biocel-aux/cell06_ker11_keep.py l.1296-1318). So dc0.20 is roughly dc0.225 plus the band [0.20, 0.225), and the two files share ~88 of 96 dummy forks. A 43/44 'plateau' is therefore not an independent replicate, and 'lone spike 44 with 43 <= 0.953' only means the extra band that 44 does NOT contain hurt. The clause cannot tell a transferable band from a few-fork coincidence. It also does not remove the winner's curse, because it still picks the maximum display. (2) The check is asymmetric. 44's other neighbour is K2 at dc0.25, which displays 0.954 and so already passes. 43's lower neighbour (0.175) is unscored. As written, the clause tests only 43 against 44. (3) Displays are rounded to 3 dp. 0.953 vs 0.954 for the neighbour can be a 1e-5..1e-4 difference around K2's own display, so the clause flips on a rounding boundary. (4) P(transfer) 0.4 vs 0.6 is a guess, the same false precision as I-092. The prior points to a flat curve anyway: sjlee's DC 0.15/0.20/0.25 all tied on public (I-018, r_ladder.json), so the clause rarely binds. (5) The value is conditional: the user must send letter (b) or (c) before the scores (default is (a)), one of 43/44 must reach >= 0.955, and the other must be <= 0.953. That is roughly 0.03-0.06 of worlds, times a guessed +1e-4..3e-4, giving an expected gain of ~1e-5. (6) 'Tie -> 44' contradicts L9's written tie order (fewer knobs, then the EARLIER submit, which is 43 at 05:28:13Z vs 44 at 05:28:22Z). Both are single-knob files. The smaller-change tiebreak is defensible but is a new class-C-only rule and must be labelled as such. Net: harmless as a conservative filter, but the claimed gain is not real.
fix: Keep the default (a), with class C only by a pre-score user letter; that already carries the risk control. If a filter is wanted anyway, write it before any 43/44 score as a documented conservative preference and claim no gain: 'a class-C ref qualifies only if every SCORED DC neighbour of it (including K2 dc0.25 = 0.954 and dc0.30 = 0.949 as context) is >= 0.954, except that dc0.30 is ignored'. In practice: 44 needs 43 >= 0.954, and 43 needs 44 >= 0.954. State openly that this is a taste for smoothness and not a transfer estimate, since the files are nested. Write the tie rule explicitly as 'class C only: tie -> 44 (fewer added forks, 88 vs 96), overriding L9's earlier-submit order', or simply use L9's order (-> 43) to avoid a new rule. Remove the P(transfer) 0.4/0.6 and the +0.0001..+0.0003 numbers from the CONTEXT entry and the brief.
realistic_gain: ~0 (expected private ~+1e-5 at most). It binds in only ~3-6% of worlds and its sign there is not established. Runtime 0.
